newsitem.title: USA: FBI seeks to question man held in Canada on bombing.
newsitem.headline: FBI seeks to question man held in Canada on bombing.

text.p: The Federal Bureau of Investigation said on Saturday it hopes to question a man being held in Canada about the bombing in Saudi Arabia that killed 19 U.S. troops last year.
Canadian immigration officials arrested Hani Abdel Rahim Hussein Al-Sayegh, 28, on Tuesday, the FBI said.
A spokesman for Canada's security service said the Saudi national had been arrested under a warrant signed by the solicitor general and the immigration minister.
The Toronto Sun reported on Saturday that Sayegh had been arrested on suspicion of being "engaged in terrorism" and being a threat to "the security of Canada."

In a statement released in Washington, the FBI said it was grateful for "the vigilant actions of Canada" and praised the government of Saudi Arabia for its "invaluable assistance leading to the identification and location of Al-Sayegh."

The Toronto newspaper, quoting unnamed sources, said Al-Sayegh was picked up at an Ottawa grocery store after a tipoff that he was a suspect in the bombing that ripped through and apartment complex in Dharan last June.
